patients.summary: Construction laborer and heavy smoker who joined in 2019 healthy; ADPKD is found in 2022, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema in 2023 and Buerger disease in 2024, and an H. pylori gastric ulcer bleeds in 2026 and heals. He keeps smoking throughout.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 31 y/o man looking for a primary care doctor. Says his last PCP retired and the replacement practice books three months out. Works construction, wants a place where he can text and get in quickly. Explained membership and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. He signed up over the phone. New patient physical booked 9/24, 8:00 am (asked for early, before a shift). Release form for prior records emailed to him.

medications.sig: 400-600 mg by mouth every 6-8 hours as needed for muscle aches (OTC)

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31M establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

No active complaints. Physically demanding job (construction laborer, mostly site prep and framing crews). Back and shoulders ache by end of week, takes OTC ibuprofen 400-600 mg when it's bad, maybe a couple of times a week.

PMH: none he knows of. PSH: tonsils out at 8. Meds: OTC ibuprofen prn only. Allergies: none to medicines.
FH: father has polycystic kidney disease and is on dialysis. Mother has emphysema/COPD, quit smoking years ago. One older brother, healthy as far as he knows.
SH: single, lives in Amherst. Cigarettes since about 19, 1 to 1.5 ppd depending on the week. No alcohol at all. No drugs.

ROS: negative in detail - no chest pain, no dyspnea, no cough beyond a morning clear-throat, no GI or GU complaints, no headaches.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing, muscular. HEENT normal, tonsils absent. Neck supple, no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, good air movement. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses felt. Ext warm, pulses 2+ radial and pedal. Skin: no rashes. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Tobacco use, ~1-1.5 ppd x 12 yrs. Talked about quitting; he's not there yet ("maybe when the season slows down"). Offered patch/varenicline whenever he wants to try. Revisit each visit.
2. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids today. One-time HIV and hep C screens. Tdap (last one he remembers was high school) and flu shot given. PHQ-2 0.
3. Muscle aches from work: OTC ibuprofen ok occasionally, with food.
4. Father's kidney disease: noted. Will keep an eye on his own BP and creatinine.

RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn. Text line explained.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nathan - all of your labs came back fine. Kidney and liver tests, blood counts and cholesterol are in normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do except keep thinking about the cigarettes. Talk soon.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 22 pages received by fax from patient's previous primary care office (visits 2012-2018). Mostly annual physicals and two sick visits for colds. BP always normal there. Labs 2016: basic metabolic and CBC normal. Childhood tonsillectomy noted. Smoking documented at every visit. No diagnoses on their problem list besides tobacco use. Indexed under Outside Records; flagged for PCP review.

documents.title: Reviewed outside records
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Nothing new. Consistent with history he gave.

documents.title: Work letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey doc, my company says we're still allowed to work since we're doing a hospital addition job. They want a letter saying I'm healthy enough to be on site with a mask. Is that something you do?

documents.title: RE: Work letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sure. Letter attached stating you have no medical restrictions for site work with the usual precautions. One honest note from me: smokers do worse with respiratory infections, and this would be a good time to cut down if you're ever going to. Stay safe out there.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Masked visit.

Has been working all through the pandemic, no COVID that he knows of. Feels fine. Still smoking, "probably closer to a pack and a half since spring, it's been a stressful year." No cough beyond usual morning, no dyspnea. Aches from work same as ever, ibuprofen a few times a week.

Meds: OTC ibuprofen prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP and weight as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext without edema. Skin normal.

A/P
- Tobacco: not ready. Gave quitline number anyway.
- BMP and CBC today. Flu vaccine given.
- PHQ-2 0.
- Follow up next fall.

documents.title: BMP, CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Normal. Released to portal with a short note.

documents.title: State registry reconciliation
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pulled state immunization registry: Pfizer COVID dose 1 4/17/21 and dose 2 5/8/21, both at a retail pharmacy. Added to immunization history.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33M annual.

Good year overall, a lot of overtime. Had both Pfizer shots in the spring, sore arm only. Smoking unchanged, 1 to 1.5 ppd. Tried cutting to half a pack in July and lasted about a week. Denies chest pain, dyspnea, cough change, abdominal pain, urinary symptoms.

NKDA. Meds: OTC ibuprofen now and then.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP normal. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart RRR. Abdomen benign. Ext warm, pulses intact.

Plan: CMP and lipids. Flu shot today. He'll get a COVID booster at the pharmacy when eligible. Discussed varenicline again: he'd consider it "after the season." PHQ-2 1 (tired from work), no concerns.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Pharmacy vaccine notification
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy notification: Pfizer COVID booster given 11/13/21. Entered.
